questions.question: Write a short note on Tuhafat-ul-Mujahiddin.
questions.solution_html:
• Tuhafat-ul-Mujahiddin is an Arabic historical work written in 1583 by Zainuddin
  • Makhdoom II of Ponnani. It records Portuguese atrocities in Malabar from 1498 to
  • 1583. The text highlights resistance by Mappila Muslims, Kunjali Marakkars and
  • the Zamorin of Calicut. It is the first authentic native source on 16th-century
  • Kerala and calls for jihad against the Portuguese.
questions.final_answer: Kerala and calls for jihad against the Portuguese
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the“Blood and Iron” policy of Marthanda Varma.
questions.solution_html:
• Marthanda Varma’s “Blood and Iron” policy meant the use of force and warfare to
  • centralise power in Travancore. He crushed the Ettuveetil Pillamar and internal
  • rivals. He modernised the army with European help under Capt. De Lannoy. The
  • policy established absolute monarchy and royal monopoly over trade.
questions.final_answer: policy established absolute monarchy and royal monopoly over trade
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on Third Anglo-Mysore War.
questions.solution_html:
• The Third Anglo-Mysore War was fought from 1790 to 1792 between Tipu Sultan
  • and the British-led alliance. Tipu’s attack on Travancore and suppression of
  • Malabar rebellions triggered the war. The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 forced
  • Tipu to cede Malabar to the British. This strengthened British control over the
  • pepper trade in Kerala.
questions.final_answer: pepper trade in Kerala
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of Paliath Achan in the anti-British resistance in Cochin.
questions.solution_html:
• Paliath Achan was the hereditary Prime Minister of Cochin. In 1808–09 Govindan
  • Achan allied with Velu Thampi against the British subsidiary alliance. He led Nair
  • forces to attack British Resident Col. Macaulay’s residence and freed prisoners.
  • The revolt was suppressed and Paliath Achan was exiled.
questions.final_answer: The revolt was suppressed and Paliath Achan was exiled
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on sambandham marital relations in Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Sambandham was a traditional non-sacramental marriage system followed by
  • Namboothiri and allied communities in matrilineal Kerala. The alliance was
  • temporary and the Nair woman stayed in her taravad. Children belonged to the
  • mother’s lineage and the husband had no property rights. The system declined
  • under colonial influence and reform movements.
questions.final_answer: under colonial influence and reform movements
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How did colonial law reinforce patriarchy in Kerala?
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial law reinforced patriarchy by applying Victorian norms to matrilineal
  • customs. The Malabar Marriage Act of 1896 and Nair Regulation of 1925 ended
  • marumakkathayam. These laws promoted nuclear families and individual male
  • property rights. They weakened women’s position in the taravad and shifted
  • society towards patriliny and monogamy.
questions.final_answer: society towards patriliny and monogamy
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a note on peition writings as a form of historical narration in Dr P / Palpu's writings.
questions.solution_html:
• Dr P Palpu used petition writings as a public form of historical narration. He
  • blended community grievances with alternative histories such as ancient
  • Buddhist Kerala versus Brahminical domination. The petitions served as tools for
  • Ezhava mobilisation and rights demands. This style became an early form of
  • modern historiography in Kerala.
questions.final_answer: modern historiography in Kerala
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse Dr P Palpu as a petition writer.
questions.solution_html:
• Dr P Palpu acted as a petition writer by submitting repeated memorials to the
  • Diwan and Viceroy. He demanded education, government jobs and temple entry
  • for Ezhavas. His writings constructed a collective Ezhava identity based on
  • historical injustice. The petitions directly paved the way for the SNDP Yogam and
  • the anti-caste movement in Travancore.
questions.final_answer: the anti-caste movement in Travancore
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the significance of Payyannur Satyagraha?
questions.solution_html:
• Payyannur Satyagraha was the 1930 Salt Satyagraha centre in Malabar led by K.
  • Kelappan. The march from Kozhikode to Payyannur broke the salt law at Uliyath
  • Kadavu. British forces raided the camp. It was called the Second Bardoli and
  • boosted the Civil Disobedience Movement across Kerala.
questions.final_answer: boosted the Civil Disobedience Movement across Kerala
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is referred to as "Niranam Pada" in the context of liberation struggle, / 1959 of Kerala?
questions.solution_html:
• “Niranam Pada” refers to the violent anti-communist militia active during the 1959
  • Vimochana Samaram in Kerala. It operated mainly in Kuttanad and was backed by
  • church and landlord interests. The group attacked communists and supporters
  • opposing land reforms. It symbolised organised resistance to the first elected
  • communist ministry.
questions.final_answer: communist ministry
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Why was Malabar district merged with Travancore-Cochin?
questions.solution_html:
• Malabar district was merged with Travancore-Cochin under the States
  • Reorganisation Act of 1956. The merger created a single Malayalam-speaking
  • Kerala state on 1 November 1956. It achieved linguistic and administrative unity
  • for the entire Malayalam region.
questions.final_answer: for the entire Malayalam region
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on the emergence of teachers’ organisations in / Malabar.
questions.solution_html:
• Teachers’ organisations emerged in Malabar in the early 20th century along with
  • western education and social reforms. Groups such as the Malabar Teachers
  • Association demanded better pay and service conditions. They linked their
  • demands to anti-feudal and nationalist struggles. Their efforts expanded public
  • education and accelerated social change.
questions.final_answer: education and accelerated social change
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse the factors that led to the Attingal Revolt against the English East / India Company.
questions.solution_html:
• The Attingal Revolt of 1721 was the first major anti-British uprising in Kerala at the
  • Anjengo factory. Economic grievances included the Company’s pepper
  • monopoly, corrupt practices and forced labour. Local chiefs rose against political
  • interference and atrocities. The British suppressed the revolt but it forced them to
  • shift focus to Travancore.
questions.final_answer: shift focus to Travancore
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate how Shakthan Thampuran consolidated political power in the / kingdom of Cochin.
questions.solution_html:
• Shakthan Thampuran consolidated power in Cochin between 1790 and 1805 by
  • ending feudal anarchy. He curbed the influence of powerful nobles including the
  • Paliath Achan. He centralised administration and planned the modern town of
  • Thrissur. He promoted the Thrissur Pooram festival to unite communities while
  • balancing British relations.
questions.final_answer: balancing British relations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate the importance of colonial exchange in shaping Kerala’s / economy
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial exchange integrated Kerala into the global capitalist economy through
  • spice exports. The shift from subsistence agriculture to cash-crop production
  • created export dependency. British agency houses and land-revenue changes
  • deepened inequalities. Infrastructure such as roads and ports developed but
  • long-term economic dependence also grew.
questions.final_answer: long-term economic dependence also grew
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss Western education as a catalytic agent of social change in / Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Western education acted as a catalytic agent of social change in Kerala from the
  • 19th century. Missionaries and the colonial state spread literacy and English
  • knowledge. It undermined caste-based traditional learning and produced new
  • reformers. The spread of education created a public sphere that fuelled anti-caste
  • movements and nationalism.
questions.final_answer: movements and nationalism
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of the janmi system under British rule.
questions.solution_html:
• The janmi system under British rule gave landlords absolute ownership rights.
  • Tenants became tenants-at-will and faced heavy exploitation. British revenue
  • policies protected janmis for political stability. This strengthened caste-class
  • hierarchy and triggered later agrarian unrest including Mappila outbreaks.
questions.final_answer: hierarchy and triggered later agrarian unrest including Mappila outbreaks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine how reform movements challenged patriarchal customs.
questions.solution_html:
• Reform movements challenged patriarchal customs through the SNDP Yogam
  • and Nair Service Society. They attacked sambandham and marumakkathayam
  • while advocating monogamy and women’s education. Leaders like Narayana Guru
  • and Chattampi Swamikal promoted gender equality. Legal changes such as the
  • Nair Regulation of 1925 gradually empowered women.
questions.final_answer: Nair Regulation of 1925 gradually empowered women
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the meaning and significance of "Kallumaala Samaram" for the / . CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Kallumaala Samaram was the 1915–16 anti-caste protest by Pulaya women in
  • Travancore. They defied dress codes by wearing stone necklaces like upper-caste
  • women. Ayyankali’s followers led the struggle for dignity. The movement became
  • a powerful symbol of lower-caste assertion and influenced later rights campaigns.
questions.final_answer: a powerful symbol of lower-caste assertion and influenced later rights campaigns
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate the challenges faced by the Travancore State Congress during / state repression.
questions.solution_html:
• The Travancore State Congress faced severe state repression after its formation in
  • 1938. Diwan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer ordered arrests, lathi charges and bans on
  • meetings. Internal divisions limited its early mass base. Sustained Satyagraha and
  • alliances eventually overcame these challenges and strengthened the demand for
  • responsible government.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) P. Ramaswami Iyer ordered arrests, lathi charges and bans on
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What led to the formation of Congress Socialist Party in Malabar.
questions.solution_html:
• The Congress Socialist Party was formed in Malabar in 1934 due to discontent with
  • moderate Congress leadership. The Great Depression and rising leftist ideas
  • accelerated the split. Leaders such as EMS Namboodiripad and A.K. Gopalan
  • pushed class-based programmes. The party radicalised the anti-feudal struggle in
  • the region.
questions.final_answer: Option K. Gopalan
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyze the shift from nationalist to class-based politics.
questions.solution_html:
• Politics in Kerala shifted from nationalist to class-based lines in the 1930s.
  • Economic distress and peasant movements against janmis drove the change. The
  • formation of the Congress Socialist Party marked the turning point. This shift
  • strengthened communism and class consciousness in Malabar.
questions.final_answer: strengthened communism and class consciousness in Malabar
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse in detail the impact of colonialism on the Princely State of / Travancore, with special reference to changes in administration, revenue system, social structure, and the overall process of state formation.
questions.solution_html:
• Colonialism profoundly impacted the Princely State of Travancore through
  • indirect rule after the 1795 subsidiary alliance. Administration was modernised
  • with a centralised bureaucracy and Dewan system. Revenue policy shifted to
  • cash-based land tax and royal monopolies on cash crops. Social structure saw
  • missionary education and reform movements that both challenged and initially
  • reinforced inequalities. Overall state formation moved from feudalism to a
  • modern princely state that later faced demands for responsible government. The
  • process combined modernisation with economic exploitation.
questions.final_answer: process combined modernisation with economic exploitation
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of colonial agrarian legislation in reinforcing caste and / class hierarchy.
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial agrarian legislation reinforced caste and class hierarchy by strengthening
  • janmi rights. Laws gave landlords absolute ownership while tenants remained
  • powerless. The Malabar Tenancy Act offered only partial relief and failed to end
  • exploitation. Upper-caste janmis retained dominance over lower-caste tenants.
  • This policy ensured colonial stability but sowed seeds for post-independence
  • land reforms and agrarian unrest.
questions.final_answer: land reforms and agrarian unrest
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Compare the goals of the Ottappalam and Payyannur conferences.
questions.solution_html:
• The Ottappalam Conference of 1921 and the Payyannur Conference of 1926 had
  • contrasting goals. Ottappalam focused on Non-Cooperation and Khilafat unity
  • with emphasis on anti-British boycott programmes. Payyannur shifted towards
  • radical peasant issues and anti-feudal demands under emerging socialist
  • influence. Ottappalam represented broad nationalist mobilisation while
  • Payyannur reflected the move to class-based politics. Together they show the
  • evolution of Congress strategy in Malabar.
questions.final_answer: evolution of Congress strategy in Malabar
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Critically evaluate the feasibility of the American Model in Travancore.
questions.solution_html:
• The American Model proposed by C.P. Ramaswami Iyer in the 1940s aimed at an
  • American-style federal democracy for independent Travancore. It promised
  • modern administration and efficient governance. However it ignored local feudal
  • and caste realities and was seen as pro-British and anti-integration. The model
  • proved unrealistic amid strong mass movements for responsible government. It
  • was ultimately rejected and Travancore joined the Indian Union in 1949. The
  • proposal symbolised elite resistance rather than genuine democratic feasibility.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) P. Ramaswami Iyer in the 1940s aimed at an
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  • strengthened communism and class consciousness in Malabar.
questions.final_answer: strengthened communism and class consciousness in Malabar
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse in detail the impact of colonialism on the Princely State of / Travancore, with special reference to changes in administration, revenue system, social structure, and the overall process of state formation.
questions.solution_html:
• Colonialism profoundly impacted the Princely State of Travancore through
  • indirect rule after the 1795 subsidiary alliance. Administration was modernised
  • with a centralised bureaucracy and Dewan system. Revenue policy shifted to
  • cash-based land tax and royal monopolies on cash crops. Social structure saw
  • missionary education and reform movements that both challenged and initially
  • reinforced inequalities. Overall state formation moved from feudalism to a
  • modern princely state that later faced demands for responsible government. The
  • process combined modernisation with economic exploitation.
questions.final_answer: process combined modernisation with economic exploitation
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of colonial agrarian legislation in reinforcing caste and / class hierarchy.
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial agrarian legislation reinforced caste and class hierarchy by strengthening
  • janmi rights. Laws gave landlords absolute ownership while tenants remained
  • powerless. The Malabar Tenancy Act offered only partial relief and failed to end
  • exploitation. Upper-caste janmis retained dominance over lower-caste tenants.
  • This policy ensured colonial stability but sowed seeds for post-independence
  • land reforms and agrarian unrest.
questions.final_answer: land reforms and agrarian unrest
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Compare the goals of the Ottappalam and Payyannur conferences.
questions.solution_html:
• The Ottappalam Conference of 1921 and the Payyannur Conference of 1926 had
  • contrasting goals. Ottappalam focused on Non-Cooperation and Khilafat unity
  • with emphasis on anti-British boycott programmes. Payyannur shifted towards
  • radical peasant issues and anti-feudal demands under emerging socialist
  • influence. Ottappalam represented broad nationalist mobilisation while
  • Payyannur reflected the move to class-based politics. Together they show the
  • evolution of Congress strategy in Malabar.
questions.final_answer: evolution of Congress strategy in Malabar
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Critically evaluate the feasibility of the American Model in Travancore.
questions.solution_html:
• The American Model proposed by C.P. Ramaswami Iyer in the 1940s aimed at an
  • American-style federal democracy for independent Travancore. It promised
  • modern administration and efficient governance. However it ignored local feudal
  • and caste realities and was seen as pro-British and anti-integration. The model
  • proved unrealistic amid strong mass movements for responsible government. It
  • was ultimately rejected and Travancore joined the Indian Union in 1949. The
  • proposal symbolised elite resistance rather than genuine democratic feasibility.
